passage_units.variant_note: Neo-Assyrian MS D instead gives king_declares_war_on_king; MS S and MS a preserve shorter Mutabal-resettlement recensions.
MS S dates the configuration to 28th Shabatu or Tashritu and differs in several outcomes; the damaged relation at IM line 10 remains unresolved.
Early Neo-Babylonian MS S transposes above and below and adds a rich-man-death and brawls clause.
MS Z gives day 15; MS S gives 14th Arahsamna and predicts an enemy incursion rather than exclusion.
MS S transposes above and below and gives a partly different apodosis in which Der prospers and its kingship endures.
MS M changes the final royal outcome to king_of_subartu_makes_peace_with_lands; MS S also changes eclipse duration.
MS S appends a separate non-calendrical favorable omen for a night that elapses during eclipse: river flood, rain, successful harvest, and good fortune.
VAT 9419+VAT 11310 preserves east wind only and a city-brightening/extinction reading; IM line 60 is corrupt where other witnesses preserve wherever cities exist devastation occurs.
Across MS Y, MS S, MS b, IM, and duplicates the boundary between protasis and apodosis changes radically; Papsukkal also varies with Sipazianna/Orion.
The edition explicitly identifies days 7 and 21 as astronomically impossible schematic dates; line 65 is not understood.

global_constraints: Rules are witness- and recension-scoped; no single harmonized canonical outcome may replace documented variants.
Month, day, darkening quadrant, clearing quadrant, watch, duration, wind, cusp state, accompanying body, and follow-up observation remain distinct predicates.
Impossible schematic eclipse dates are preserved as textual facts and never treated as computable astronomical events.
Supplementary fixed-star and planetary omens remain separate from the calendrical eclipse protasis they accompany.
All political, military, death, famine, flood, destruction, and ritual implications are historical evidence only.
No rule accepts birth data, creates a natal delineation, or produces customer predictions.
